blocks: Control Change numbers 120–127 change how a channel behaves rather than a sound parameter: All Sound Off, Reset All Controllers, Local Control, All Notes Off, and the Omni, Mono and Poly modes. MIDI/CC lists them.
MIDI/SysEx — System Exclusive (F0h … F7h): a message of any length whose content a manufacturer defines, used for preset dumps, firmware and device-specific commands.
Song Position Pointer (F2h) — where in the song to resume, counted in sixteenth notes. See MIDI/Clock.
MIDI Time Code Quarter Frame (F1h), Song Select (F3h) and Tune Request (F6h) complete the group.
MIDI/Clock — Timing Clock (F8h), 24 per quarter note, with Start (FAh), Continue (FBh) and Stop (FCh).
Active Sensing (FEh) — an optional signal that the connection is alive. A receiver that has heard one and then hears nothing for 300 ms turns its voices off.
Reset (FFh) — returns every receiver to its power-up state.
Real-time messages may arrive in the middle of other messages, including a long SysEx dump, so the clock stays steady.
The Launchpad Pro MK3 sends Note On with velocity 0 as its Note Off (Launchpad/PRG/03 MIDI).
The MicroFreak's Filter knob sends CC 23 (Microfreak/UG/17 Ext Gear/09 MIDI CC Control).
Renaming a MicroFreak preset over USB takes SysEx messages, then a Program Change to select the renamed preset (Microfreak/CLI/Preset metadata over USB).
Ableton Live sends Clock and Song Position Pointer to keep external gear in time (Ableton/Live/UG/37 Sync with Link Tempo Follower and MIDI/03 Synchronizing via MIDI).
MIDI is not audio. A MIDI file or clip holds instructions. The sound comes from whatever instrument receives them.
Not every control is a CC. Pitch bend, aftertouch and program change are message types of their own, so a mapping that listens for CCs doesn't see them.
MPE is not a new message type. MIDI Polyphonic Expression gives each sounding note its own channel, so channel-wide messages such as Pitch Bend, Channel Pressure and CC 74 shape one note at a time.

The pair of MIDI/Message types that start and end a note: Note On (90h–9Fh) and Note Off (80h–8Fh). Each carries a note number and a velocity, both 0–127.
The note number picks the pitch. 60 is middle C, Music/Note/4/C, and each step is a semitone. Note pages in this garden record it as Logseq/Entity/Music/Note/Frontmatter/midi-note.
Velocity is how hard the key was struck. A Note On with velocity 0 counts as a Note Off, and some devices send it in place of one, as the Launchpad Pro MK3 does (Launchpad/PRG/03 MIDI).
A receiver pairs each Note Off with the last Note On for the same note number on the same channel. A lost Note Off leaves a stuck note, which All Notes Off (MIDI/CC 123) clears.
Notes can trigger more than pitches. Live can map a note to a button or switch (Ableton/Live/UG/34 MIDI and Key Remote/02 The Mapping Browser/02 Mapping to MIDI Notes).
A MIDI/Message (E0h–EFh) that sends the position of the pitch bend wheel or lever as one value from 0 to 16,383, split across two data values.
8,192 (2000h) is the center, with no bend. Lower values bend down and higher values bend up.
The message doesn't say how far a full bend goes; the receiver decides. A sender can set the range with RPN 0 on MIDI/CC, and General MIDI makes ±2 semitones the default.
Pitch Bend applies to the whole channel. MPE gives each note its own channel so each can bend on its own.
A MIDI/Message (C0h–CFh) that selects a preset, called a program or patch, by number 0–127. Menus often show it as 1–128.
To reach past 128 presets, a sender first sends Bank Select on MIDI/CC 0, and 32 for the fine half, then the Program Change.
The MicroFreak selects a preset with CC 0 and a Program Change (Microfreak/Q/In the Microfreak, is there any documented way to send a MIDI message that would engage sequence B?).
A MIDI clip in Ableton Live can send a bank and program change when it launches (Ableton/Live/UG/08 Clip View/03 Extended Clip Properties/02 MIDI Clip Bank and Program Change Controls).

Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?
Short answer: use the controllers the MIDI spec marks "Undefined": 3, 9, 14, 15, 20–31, 85–87, 89, 90 and 102–119. The block 102–119 is the largest run.
Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?

Avoid 120–127. These are Channel Mode Messages, which "affect the channel's operating mode" rather than a sound parameter: All Sound Off, Reset All Controllers, Local Control On/Off, All Notes Off, Omni Off, Omni On, Mono On and Poly On.
Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?
88 is not free. It is High Resolution Velocity Prefix, between the undefined 85–87 and 89–90.
Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?
Check the controller's own defaults too. The Launchpad Pro's Custom 2 faders send CC 15–22 (Launchpad/UG/08 Custom Modes/02 Default Custom Modes), which overlaps the undefined 15 and 20–22.
Which MIDI CC numbers are free for custom mappings?
Example: Launchpad/Custom/1/Arrangement uses CC 116–119 on channel 16. Launchpad/Custom/1/Ableton-Ctrl uses 114 and 115 on the same channel, leaving 102–113 free.

System Exclusive — a MIDI/Message whose content a manufacturer defines. It opens with F0h and a manufacturer ID, carries any number of data values from 0 to 127, and closes with F7h.
A receiver that doesn't recognize the ID ignores the rest. That lets each maker add its own commands for preset dumps, firmware updates and settings no standard message covers.
The IDs 7Eh and 7Fh belong to no manufacturer and carry Universal SysEx messages. Device Inquiry, which asks a device to identify itself, is one (Launchpad/PRG/03 MIDI/01 Device Inquiry).
Only real-time messages such as MIDI/Clock may arrive in the middle of a SysEx message.

The smallest self-contained program or dataset that reliably reproduces a bug, allowing someone else to copy, run, and observe the same problem without any additional context.
Minimal — include only what is necessary to demonstrate the problem; remove everything unrelated.
Complete — include everything someone else needs to run it; no external dependencies or missing setup.
Reproducible — verify it actually triggers the issue before sharing.
Coined and popularized by the Stack Overflow community; the canonical reference is the Stack Overflow Help Center: How to create a Minimal, Reproducible Example.

Also known by several older acronyms: MCVE (Minimal, Complete, Verifiable Example), MWE (Minimal Working Example), SSCCE (Short, Self Contained, Correct Example), and reprex (reproducible example, common in the R community).
Creating one is useful both for getting help (forces clarity) and for diagnosing the problem yourself — the process of stripping code down often reveals the root cause.

Claude Code has extremely elaborate prompts filled with heuristics, examples and IMPORTANT (tch-tch) reminders. The system prompt is ~2800 tokens long, with the Tools taking up a whopping 9400 tokens. The user prompt always contains the claude.md file, which can typically be another 1000-2000 tokens. The system prompt contains sections on tone, style, proactiveness, task management, tool usage policy and doing tasks. It also contains the date, current working directory, platform and OS information and recent commits.

One of the major patterns most coding agent creators have settled on is the context file (aka Cursor Rules / claude.md / agent.md). The difference in Claude Code's performance with and without claude.md is night and day. It is a great way for the developers to impart context that cannot be inferred from the codebase and to codify all strict preferences. For example, you can force the LLM to skip some folders, or use specific libraries. CC sends the entire contents of the claude.md with every user request
